case_name: Edmund S. Lyngdoh and another v State of Meghalaya and another
respondent:
State of Meghalaya and another
Supreme Court of India

16 September 2014
Cr.A. No. 2056 of 2014 (Arising out of S.L.P. (Cr.) No. 553/2011) with Cr.A. Nos. 2057-58 of 2014 (Arising out of S.L.P. (Cr.) Nos. 2203-2204/2011)
The Judgment was delivered by : R. Banumathi, J.
1. Leave granted.
2. These appeals arising out of SLP (Crl.) Nos. 2203-2204/2011 are filed challenging the judgment of the Gauhati High Court confirming the conviction of the appellant-first accused (Deva Prasad Sharma) u/s. 420 IPC, 120B IPC and S. 5(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 (for short 'the P.C. Act') and enhancement of the sentence imposed on him. Fourth accused (Edmund S. Lyngdoh) has preferred SLP (Crl.) No.553/2011 challenging the reversal of his acquittal and assailing the conviction u/s. 420 IPC read with Section 120B IPC.
3. Deva Prasad Sharma (A-1) died on 9.10.2011 during the pendency of the petition before this Court and his legal representative was brought on re
facts: The case involves a procurement scam at North Eastern Hill University, Shillong, where Deva Prasad Sharma (A-1) colluded with others to procure Damp Seal Cement from fictitious firms at an exorbitant rate.
Deva Prasad Sharma (A-1) was the Chief Engineer of NEHU and Technical Member in the Purchase Committee.
The case was investigated by CBI, and charges were framed against A-1 to A-5 under various sections of IPC and PC Act.
The trial court convicted A-1 and sentenced him to imprisonment, while A-2 to A-5 were acquitted.
The High Court enhanced the punishment imposed on A-1 and dismissed his appeal.
issues: Whether Deva Prasad Sharma (A-1) induced the Purchase Committee to approve the rates of two firms at an inflated rate?
Whether there was sufficient evidence to prove that A-1 misled the Purchase Committee?
petitioner_arguments: There is no evidence to show that A-1 had induced the Purchase Committee to approve the rates of two firms M/s Premiere Enterprises and M/s Edmund S. Lyngdoh (fourth accused) at the rate of Rs.42.75 per kg.
The contract was awarded to the lowest tenderer, and there was no question of A-1 inducing the Purchase Committee by deception.
respondent_arguments: Quotations were floated by A-1 even prior to the matter being taken up by the Purchase Committee, and as Chief Engineer, he must have known the then prevailing market rate.
Adequate evidence has been adduced by the prosecution to bring home the guilt of A-1 that he induced the Purchase Committee to purchase DPC at an inflated rate.
court_reasoning: The trial court and High Court recorded concurrent findings of fact that before ever the Purchase Committee approved the rate, quotations were already invited by A-1.

The role of the Technical Members in the Purchase Committee becomes vital and important, and it was expected that they would contribute their technical knowledge and give their best possible opinion, suggestion, and advice to the Purchase Committee.
holding: The appeals are dismissed. The judgment of the High Court is upheld.
cases_cited: Edmund S. Lyngdoh and another v State of Meghalaya
